The Naso, also called Teribe, are an Indigenous people of the Teribe River in Bocas del Toro, northwest Panama, near the border with Costa Rica. They speak a Chibchan language. They are one of the few peoples of the Americas still led by a king.

They farm, fish and hunt in the forested valley. In the late 1600s and 1700s Spanish friars moved some of them over the mountains to Térraba in Costa Rica, where their descendants still live. Their neighbours include the Bribri and the Ngäbe and Buglé.

A hydroelectric dam on their river caused conflict in the 2000s. In 2020 Panama created the Naso Tjër Di comarca, a self-governed territory for them.
